To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
PM is the process of managing the performance of individuals, teams, and organizations to achieve the desired objectives of the organization.
the Nepalese organizations should develop a four-column model comprising of HRD context and issues, PM context and issues, and the HRD structure and roles for PM.
PM and HRD are closely linked and that HRD is a prerequisite for the success of any PM system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new model of HRD for PM.
the relationship between HRD and PM, and the development of a four-column model for PM and HRD.
the development of HRD for PM and the creation of a learning environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PM and HRD are interrelated, and the development of a learning environment can help organizations to manage performance and achieve their objectives.
HRD is an important factor in improving PM and that the HRD function needs to develop new roles and structures in order to improve PM.
PM and HRD are two sides of the same coin, which are interdependent and complementary.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the paper is the first to develop a four-column model of PM and HRD for Nepalese organizations.
the HRD professionals in Nepal need to be trained and educated to understand the concept of performance management and its importance to the organization.
the HRD and PM issues are interlinked.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HRD and PM are closely interlinked and should be managed together in order to achieve the organization's goals.
the Nepalese context is unique in that it is a developing economy with a strong cultural influence.
Nepalese organizations should focus on the development of human resources and performance management in order to compete in the global market.
